answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a costly, slow-to-earn reputation bond before it can transact — like tending an orchard, not planting a flag. A new agent must complete a long sequence of small, verifiable jobs while a falcon-eyed peer review samples its work; cloning the identity means redoing the whole season of labour from scratch, and the bond is slashed if fraud is found. Cheap marble tokens alone prove nothing — only time, work, and forfeitable stake make a thousand fake agents cost a thousand real efforts.
